Vacuum Maze

An apparatus for the extraction of single atoms from laboratory tubing, after Knudsen (1909)

One cold atom is loose in a maze of stainless-steel vacuum pipe. Tip the apparatus (your phone) and real gravity pulls it along. It doesn't bounce like a marble: it sticks to the steel for a moment, then leaves at a random angle (Knudsen's cosine law) with the wall's temperature. Steer it into a vacuum pump.

Begin opens Level 0, a short run to the pump. Skip any time. Nothing is recorded.

Every element plays at a similar speed, because its wall temperature is set by its mass. Heavier atoms are drawn bigger, although real atomic size doesn't follow mass. The last column is each element's cooling line. Cooling lasers unlock in the editor (and the official mazes) with the cold-atom chapters — a free update — and each element answers only to its own laser colours.
